points.text: The Selic was cut to 13.75% on 16 September, the fifth straight quarter-point cut from 15%.
September's IPCA-15 surprised higher at 0.70%, and 12-month inflation is 4.47%, just under the 4.5% ceiling.
The external position is strong. Reserves were $368.9bn in July.
The 12-month current account deficit was 2.71% of GDP through March.
This is the core issue for Brazil. Gross debt reached 82.5% of GDP in July, the highest since April 2021.
Twelve-month interest costs total 8.67% of GDP. The 12-month nominal deficit reached 9.99% of GDP in June.
No IMF programme. Domestic funding runs through NTN-Fs (fixed-rate), NTN-Bs (IPCA-linked) and LFTs (Selic-linked). The curve section in Valuation below comes straight from Tesouro Direto every day.
One EM strategist moved Brazil USD sovereigns to Underweight as a valuation call, arguing spreads have richened to near one-year tights while fiscal evidence has not improved.
DI futures (B3) have no free API, so the DI×pré swap reference rate from BCB is shown as a proxy.
The catalyst is the election: first round on October 4 and runoff on October 25.

events.label: IMF EFF expires. What replaces it?

points.text: The CBE held rates on 24 September, with the discount rate at 19.50%.
Headline inflation eased to 14.3% in June, but the IMF expects it to rise to 16.7% in H2 2026, which delays convergence to target by about a year.
Net international reserves reached $57.2bn at end-August, and remittances hit $47.3bn in FY2025/26.
The current account deficit is estimated at 4.5% of GDP for FY2025/26, and gross reserves were 119% of the IMF's ARA metric at end-June.
Egypt is the textbook case of an interest burden. Interest payments reached 11% of GDP in FY2024/25.
A rights-group analysis of the 2025/26 budget found interest equal to about 87% of expected tax revenue.
On the other side, the primary surplus is projected to rise from 4.8% to 5% of GDP in FY2026/27, and the government is targeting debt/GDP of 78% by June 2027.
Refinancing is the key risk for a pitch. The CBE projects 2026 external debt service of $29.18bn.
Total external debt was $161.2bn at end-September 2025, with 19.2% of it short-term.
IMF: completing the seventh EFF review unlocked about $1.8bn, bringing total disbursements to about $7.3bn. The EFF has been extended through December 15, 2026.
Add Eurobond and T-bill yields to the bonds list. USD bond prices have no free API.
The EFF runs to December 15, 2026. What replaces it is a catalyst worth flagging.

nigeria.name: Nigeria
nigeria.bonds_label: FGN bonds, DMO price sheet (yield levels match the USD Eurobond curve)

points.text: GDP grew 4.43% year-on-year in Q2 2026, up from 3.89% in Q1 and 4.23% a year earlier.
Headline inflation eased to 15.39% in August from 15.43% in July, the third straight monthly slowdown. Core inflation fell to 13.29%, its lowest since March 2021.

The policy rate is 26.5%, so the real policy rate is roughly +11%, which is very high. The next MPC is expected to want clearer evidence of sustained disinflation before cutting, even though the case for easing has strengthened.
This is the standout. Gross reserves rose $12.76bn year-on-year to $54.61bn as of 14 September 2026, a 30.5% increase, and they are already above the CBN's full-year projection of about $51.04bn.
The naira strengthened from about ₦1,368/$ at end-July to around ₦1,315/$ in early September.

This is the weak spot, and the interest/revenue metric captures it. Based on the 2026–28 MTEF, annualised 2025 revenue of about N23.43trn compared with debt service of N16.26trn, a debt service-to-revenue ratio of about 61%.
Total public debt was N166.79trn at 30 June 2026, of which 54.91% was domestic.
Nigeria has no IMF programme. Moody's has upgraded it to B3.
On the DMO sheet dated 22 September, yields run from 5.749% on the Nov 2027 bond to 8.206% on the Sep 2051. The Feb 2032 yields 6.837% and the Dec 2034 yields 7.403%.
The next MPC: a first cut depends on clearer evidence of sustained disinflation.

points.text: The Bank of Ghana held the policy rate at 14% for a third straight meeting.
Q2 GDP grew 6%, and inflation rose to 5% in August from 4.6%. That is below the 6–10% target band.
The trade surplus was $8.85bn in the first eight months of 2026, and reserves were $12bn as of September 22, or 4.5 months of imports.
Note the volatility, though: reserves had fallen to $11.07bn in August, a 12-month low, down about $1.9bn from June.
The current account surplus was 7.9% of GDP in 2025, supported by historically high gold prices. That is a concentration risk to flag.
IMF staff see lowering the primary surplus to 0.5% of GDP from 2027 as consistent with debt sustainability.
The IMF completed the final ECF review, and Ghana's risk of debt distress was upgraded to moderate, two years earlier than expected.
IMF engagement is moving to a non-financing PCI.

Watch the PCI approval, gold prices and whether BoG cuts given inflation below the target band.

events.label: Fuel-tax suspension and zero-rated VAT expire
Bank of Zambia MPC (a cut is possible)

points.text: Inflation eased to 6.1% in September, its lowest since February 2018.
One watch item: the fuel-tax suspension and zero-rated VAT expire on September 30.
The Bank of Zambia could cut again on 30 September after a 25bp cut in May took the policy rate to 13.25%. The IMF has revised 2026 growth down to 4.3%.
Reserves are $6.4bn, or 4.4 months of prospective imports. The current account is expected to move to a surplus of 1.5% of GDP.

The primary surplus is now projected at 1.1% of GDP for 2026, down from 3.8% at the sixth review. The IMF blamed weaker tax collection, pre-election spending, a wage adjustment and agricultural subsidy overruns.
Restructuring agreements now cover 94% of eligible debt.
The government says annual external debt service falls below $900m, and it completed a buyback of the remaining $1.36bn 2053 Eurobond using $600m of AfDB concessional financing.
Add post-restructuring Eurobond yields to the bonds list.
Hichilema was re-elected with about 60% of the vote. Talks on a successor IMF programme are expected to resume with the new government, and a new programme deal is the obvious near-term catalyst.
